metric.name: frame_p95_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur, a.jank_type
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  frames AS (
    SELECT * FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT dur AS ns, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY dur) AS rank, count(*) OVER () AS n
    FROM frames
  )
SELECT (SELECT ns / 1e6 FROM ranked WHERE rank = (n * 95 + 99) / 100) AS value

claims.text: The selected UI-frame p95 metric improved from 76.544292 ms in baseline to 73.255125 ms in current, a delta of -3.289167 ms; this is not a frame-time regression.

claims.text: The trace-localized binder wait did increase on the app's UI thread, but it is a whole-trace aggregate: synchronous calls to SurfaceFlinger rose from 371 calls and 287.81833 ms to 400 calls and 348.319381 ms while the number of recorded frames also rose from 746 to 834.

INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.binder;
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  main_thread AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ui_thread_utid AS utid FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  )
SELECT server_process, count(*) AS txn_count, sum(client_dur) / 1e6 AS wait_ms
FROM android_binder_txns
WHERE is_sync AND client_dur > 0 AND client_utid IN (SELECT utid FROM main_thread)
GROUP BY server_process
ORDER BY wait_ms DESC

caveats: This conclusion is based on one capture per side; small aggregate differences can be run-to-run noise.
The increased binder total is not normalized per frame, and the current capture contains more recorded frames, so it is not sufficient evidence of a UI-frame regression.
